summary: DIRECTER proposes a plausibility-guided decoding loop that dynamically modulates KV-cache key-scaling strength per decoding step, using a one-time attention-sensitivity layer ranking to progressively weaken steering when the steered distribution deviates from the raw one. The problem (oversteering in activation steering) is real and well-motivated, the method is simple and practical, and the evaluation spans three benchmarks, five models across two families, meaningful ablations, robustness sweeps, efficiency measurements, and LLM/human-judged generation quality. The main weaknesses are the absence of error bars or significance testing on the main tables, a narrow set of steering baselines (only PASTA and SpotLight, while cited dynamic-steering works are never compared empirically), and reliance on gpt-4o-mini both for rewriting IFEval prompts and judging output quality. Overall this is a sound, useful, borderline-accept contribution with fixable evidentiary gaps.
strengths: Well-motivated and cleanly designed method: the plausibility constraint (Eq. 1) plus progressive halving of steered layers is a simple, training-free mechanism that directly targets the documented oversteering failure of prior steering methods.

Broad empirical coverage for a paper of this type: three benchmarks (IFEval, LIFBench, GSM8K-Format), five models from 1B to 14B across Llama and Qwen families, plus ablations on fixed vs. dynamic strength, reversed/random layer ranking, random token spans, beta/alpha robustness, and prompt-template robustness.

Evidence that gains do not trade off generation quality: Table 4 shows DIRECTER matches non-intervention text quality while achieving the highest task fidelity (~92%), corroborated by a human evaluation (Appendix E.3).

The plausibility filter is shown to transfer as a safety gate to other steering methods (Figure 2b), supporting the claim that it is a general anti-oversteering mechanism rather than a method-specific trick.

Efficiency is honestly quantified (~16% throughput reduction, negligible memory, 2x faster than SpotLight) and the gating mechanism that skips unnecessary steered passes is a thoughtful practical contribution.

key_concerns.issue: No statistical rigor on the main results: Tables 1, 2, and 4 report single-run numbers with no seeds, error bars, or significance tests. Only the random-layer/token ablations report variance (±0.7, ±1.1), and several key margins (e.g., 61.3→61.6 on Llama-3.2-1B, 81.6→83.5 on Qwen-2.5-14B) are small enough that their reality is unestablished. Greedy decoding removes sampling variance but not dataset/seed-level uncertainty.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over multiple evaluation seeds/prompt-order shuffles (or bootstrap CIs over examples) for all main tables, and add paired significance tests for the headline comparisons vs. zero-shot and tuned steering baselines.

key_concerns.issue: The steering baseline set is thin: only PASTA and SpotLight are compared, while the paper itself cites several dynamic/adaptive steering methods (Lee et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025; Postmus & Abreu, 2024) that are never evaluated. The claim of surpassing 'prior steering methods by ~4%' rests on two baselines whose tuned configurations were selected by the authors.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one recent adaptive/dynamic steering baseline, or clearly scope the superiority claim to attention-level steering methods and justify the omission.

key_concerns.issue: Potential circularity in evaluation: IFEval prompts are rewritten by gpt-4o-mini and generation quality/task fidelity are also judged by gpt-4o-mini, with no reported validation of the rewriting step or judge agreement rates. Additionally, GSM8K-Format is an author-constructed benchmark, which risks (even unintentionally) favoring the proposed method.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report human verification of a sample of rewritten IFEval prompts, disclose judge prompts and agreement with human labels, and include at least one fully external formatting-constraint benchmark or release enough of GSM8K-Format's construction to allow independent audit.

key_concerns.issue: The plausibility criterion uses only the top-1 token of the raw distribution with a fixed beta=0.5; while robustness to beta is shown, the choice of top-1 (rather than top-k mass or KL-based deviation) is heuristic and only weakly justified.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Ablate the plausibility criterion itself (top-k probability mass, KL/JSD threshold) to show the top-1 rule is not a fragile design point.

key_concerns.issue: The trailing standalone LIMITATIONS section is generic boilerplate ('we have not isolated every factor...') that adds nothing beyond the specific, useful limitations already stated in the Conclusion, and slightly undercuts the paper's otherwise good calibration.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Replace the boilerplate with the concrete limitations (heuristic sensitivity metric, separable instruction-span assumption, limited baseline set) already identified in the Conclusion.

key_concerns.issue: Sensitivity ranking requires a per-prompt one-time analysis whose cost is only partially characterized; the worst-case short-generation regime is acknowledged but the absolute overhead in latency for typical IFEval-length generations is deferred to an appendix.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State the absolute one-time ranking cost (seconds per prompt) in the main text alongside the throughput figures.

questions_for_authors: How many evaluation runs/seeds underlie Tables 1, 2, and 4, and what is the bootstrap confidence interval on the headline +6.5% average improvement and the small gains on Llama-3.2-1B and Qwen-2.5-14B?
Why were the cited dynamic steering methods (Lee et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025; Postmus & Abreu, 2024) not included as baselines, and how does DIRECTER compare to at least one of them?
What fraction of gpt-4o-mini-rewritten IFEval prompts were human-verified, and what is the agreement between the gpt-4o-mini judge and the human annotators in Appendix E.3?
How sensitive is DIRECTER to the plausibility criterion itself — e.g., using top-k cumulative probability or a KL threshold instead of the top-1 rule in Eq. 1?
What is the absolute wall-clock cost of the one-time sensitivity analysis per prompt, and how does it scale with prompt length and layer count?
Baselines were tuned on IFEval and applied elsewhere; was beta=0.5 for DIRECTER selected using any benchmark data, and if so, which?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly well-scoped — the 'up to 6.5%' and '~4% over prior steering' figures match Table 1, and limitations are stated — but the generality claim over 'prior steering methods' outruns the two-baseline evidence, and small per-model gains are asserted without variance estimates.

significance.justification: A practical, training-free fix for a recognized oversteering problem that practitioners of activation steering would likely adopt, but the impact is incremental rather than field-shifting.

novelty.justification: The per-step plausibility-gated modulation of steered-layer count is a genuinely new combination, though its components (KV-cache scaling, plausibility/contrastive decoding, quantization-style sensitivity analysis) are adapted from existing ideas.

rigor.justification: The method is valid and the ablations isolate the key design choices (dynamic vs. fixed strength, ranking direction, token span), but the top-1 plausibility rule and fixed beta are heuristic and the claim–evidence link for small gains is weak.

statistical_soundness.justification: No seeds, error bars, or significance tests on any main table; only the random ablations report variance, leaving several headline margins (some under 2 points) statistically unestablished.

calibration_honesty.justification: Headline numbers match the tables, trade-offs and worst-case efficiency are disclosed, and concrete limitations are stated, though the '~4% over prior steering' claim rests on only two baselines and one limitations section is boilerplate.

clarity.justification: The paper is well organized with a clear algorithm, explicit research questions, and an intuitive Figure 1 caption, though the notation around the disturbance score (Eq. 2) is dense and some justification is deferred to appendices.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure (Intro, Related Work, Method, Experiments with explicit RQs, Analyses, Conclusion with limitations) at a reasonable length.

reproducibility.justification: Algorithm, hyperparameters (alpha=100, beta=0.5), decoding settings, datasets, and baseline tuning procedure are all described in the main text with appendix pointers; the method could be reimplemented from the text alone.

related_work.justification: Prior steering work is fairly and accurately characterized with clear delineation, but several cited dynamic-steering methods are discussed only rhetorically and never compared empirically.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative, claim-supporting displays (method overview, fixed-strength and compatibility ablations, beta/alpha/prompt robustness, efficiency), each tied to a stated RQ rather than decorative.

breadth_generality.justification: Three benchmarks, five models across two families, and a transfer experiment to other methods support moderate generality, but only two steering baselines, one main analysis model, and an author-built benchmark limit the strength of the generality claims.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a sound, useful, well-presented method whose acceptance case hinges on adding variance/significance reporting and at least one stronger adaptive-steering baseline.
